findings.claim: The `invalid_union` branch reads `issue.options`, a property that does not exist on Zod v4's `$ZodIssueInvalidUnion` (which carries `errors`), so this discriminator-specific branch is likely dead code and the reworded string is never emitted.
findings.rationale: In zod v4 the union issue shape is `{ code: 'invalid_union', errors: $ZodIssue[][] }`; discriminator value lists are reported via `invalid_value`/`values`. If `options` is never populated, the guard always fails and the function falls through to the generic "Вуруди нодуруст", meaning this translation fix has no observable effect. Medium confidence — worth verifying against the actual issue type and against how other locales (e.g. en.ts) format union errors; the fact that the code needs `Array.isArray` plus a truthiness guard suggests the author was unsure of the shape too.

findings.claim: `${o}` interpolation of union option values will render objects as `[object Object]` and lose quoting fidelity for non-string primitives.
findings.rationale: If `options` ever does contain non-string values (numbers, `null`, objects, symbols would even throw on implicit string conversion), the produced message is unhelpful or, for symbols, a TypeError. Using `JSON.stringify`/`util.inspect`-style formatting as other locales do would be safer. Low-to-medium confidence since it depends on the actual runtime shape of `options`.
